jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor (fixed-term) in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a fixed-term Assistant Professor position in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics, in the group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen. The position is for four years, open from as soon as possible; a later start in 2027 can be negotiated.

Professor Mikkelsen's group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk second-order nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group's experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI's new building. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

The Assistant Professor will lead an independent research direction within the group’s programme on light–matter interaction in nanocavities. Directions of particular interest include:

• 
Cavity QED with few emitters — strong coupling with exactly one, two or several quantum emitters in deterministically fabricated nanogaps, the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and quantum light generation from nanocavity-coupled emitters

• 
Quantum and two-dimensional materials in nanogaps — out-of-plane excitations (interlayer excitons, dark excitons, trions) coupled to the vertical field of a nanogap at cryogenic temperatures and in vector magnetic fields; optically dressed states of 2D semiconductors and magnets driven inside a nanogap and read out by single-cavity ultrafast spectroscopy

• 
Ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics — time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, time-varying cavities, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients

 Candidates are expected to define their own experimental programme within this scope, and proposals that cut across these directions are welcome.

This is a leadership position for an early-career scientist ready for independence. The Assistant Professor will be the senior scientist in the group alongside Professor Mikkelsen, with day-to-day responsibility for one research direction and its students. The successful candidate will take scientific ownership of the group's new cryogenic and ultrafast facilities, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet and a tunable femtosecond laser system, co-supervise PhD and master's students, and develop their own funding portfolio, with active support from the group and the institute. They will be supported in applying as principal investigator for Danish and European early-career grants, and the position includes a dedicated budget line for a student and consumables. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

We seek an outstanding experimentalist, typically three to seven years after the PhD, with a strong publication record, demonstrated independence, and hands-on expertise in several of: nanophotonics, cavity QED or plasmonics; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy; ultrafast pump–probe spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Expertise in the exfoliation, transfer, assembly and encapsulation of van der Waals heterostructures, including gated devices, is an asset. Experience supervising students and an interest in teaching are expected. The group is simultaneously recruiting postdoctoral researchers; candidates may apply to both positions.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, funded by external research grants, and is not tenure-track. The objective is that the successful candidate concludes the appointment with an established research direction, an independent funding record, and a strong case for a permanent position at the University of Copenhagen or elsewhere.

The assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within quantum optics and photonics. To a limited extent this may also include performance of other duties. 

Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

At Factbird, we help manufacturers see what’s really happening on their lines, so they can make better, faster decisions. Our plug-and-play hardware and cloud platform turn live production data into clear insights, and we’re scaling fast across sites, teams, and countries.

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

About the role

Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

The team mission we are on: Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

What You'll Do

• Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how

• Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.

• Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.

• Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes

• Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.

• Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.

• Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.

• Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.

• Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.

• Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.

• Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

About you

You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”

You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.

You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:

• A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).

• Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.

• Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.

• Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.

• Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.

• Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.

• Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.

• A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

We’d love to hear from you

If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Khristel, our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead at khma@factbird.com

jobs.occupation: Fully funded PhD position in Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies
jobs.description:
The Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies in the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a full-time three-year PhD scholarship, with an expected starting date of 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD project will be part of the research project Sensing Korea: Reframing Korean Studies in the Nordic Countries, funded by the Academy of Korean Studies. Sensing Korea aims to develop sensory and narrative approaches to Korean Studies in order to explore the diversity of Korean experiences beyond essentializing representations.

  The PhD scholarship is funded through the Core University Program for Korean Studies of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the Korean Studies Promotion Service at the Academy of Korean Studies (AKS-2026-OLU-2250001). Sensing Korea is led by Barbara Wall and hosted by Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, University of Copenhagen. The project runs for five years, from June 2026 to May 2031.

  The PhD candidate will be supervised by project leader Barbara Wall and will work closely with a project team comprising scholars based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies as well as researchers from Korean Studies programs at other Nordic universities. The candidate is also expected to have an interest in communicating academic knowledge about Korea to a broader public.

  About the department
 The project is based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, which is part of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. The department has approximately 800 students and 150 employees. At the department, we research and teach in language, culture, religion and society, primarily with a focus on regions outside Western Europe and the USA. The work is rooted in language-based area studies and cross-cultural perspectives that provide insight into global contexts and cultural complexity.

  Introduction to the PhD programme
 PhD studies consist of research programmes that qualify students for independent and wide-ranging research, development and teaching at international level. The main emphasis is on PhD students organising and conducting their own research project (under supervision). The programme culminates in the submission of a PhD thesis, which the student must defend in public. The programme is prescribed to 180 ECTS points, corresponding to three years of full-time study. The PhD will have to teach and carry out other tasks at the department as part of the PhD position corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months).

  A PhD opens up a range of career opportunities in academia and elsewhere. As well as writing a thesis, PhD students work in active research environments in Denmark and abroad. They contribute to the academic environment, take research training courses and convey the results of their research in teaching, at academic conferences and to the general public. 

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to a master’s degree in Korean Studies or a related field in the humanities. Particularly relevant disciplinary backgrounds and research interests include Literary Studies and Sensory Studies, as well as Musicology, Media Studies, Religious Studies, Cultural Studies, History, Art History/Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and East Asian Studies. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Korean Studies or a related humanities discipline, with research interests in Literary Studies and/or Sensory Studies, or in another relevant field with a clear connection to sensory and narrative approaches to Korea. Excellent proficiency in Korean and English is essential. Proficiency in a Scandinavian language and/or Literary Sinitic (Hanmun) is considered an advantage.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we will obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency. Applicants must possess skills in written and spoken academic English at a high level. Additional language skills and knowledge of related regions is an advantage. If deemed necessary, the department may request that applicants document their English or other language skills.

  Application
 All applications must be submitted online, in PDF or Microsoft Word format, via the link “Apply for the position” at the bottom of the page. 

  The application must include: 

  Personal statement (max. one page)
 In their personal statements, applicants are encouraged to: 

   	
• outline how the PhD project relates to other research activities at the department, particularly the Sensing Korea project.  	
• describe as clearly as possible their competencies and personal qualifications relevant to the PhD programme and the Sensing Korea project.   CV
 Applications must be accompanied by a CV (max.one page) and a list of publications, where relevant. 

  Documentation (diplomas and transcripts) 
 Applicants must upload the following:

   	
• A copy of their Master’s degree diploma or similar (if this is not available by the application deadline, applicants must document pre-approval of their Master’s thesis) 	
• A copy of their Master’s degree transcript 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree diploma 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree transcript.   Applicants with a degree from a university where the working language is not English or one of the Scandinavian languages must submit a translation of their Master’s diploma and/or diploma transcripts approved by the issuing university of by another local authority. These documents must be translated into English, Danish, Norwegian or Swedish. An official description of the grading scale (and a diploma supplement where relevant) must also be attached. 

  Chinese applicants must attach a China Credentials Verification (CHSI) certificate. Read more about CHSI here: https://www.chsi.com.cn/xlcx/en/index.jsp.

  Project description 
 Applications must include a preliminary project description covering the problem formulation, overall objectives, methodology, design and timetable (max. five pages/12,000 characters, incl. spaces, excl. bibliography). The project description should also give a preliminary indication of what research literature the candidate would expect to engage with. 
 
 On the website of the PhD School, you can find more information about the attachments your need to include with your application:PhD at the Faculty of Humanities – University of Copenhagen / https://phd.humanities.ku.dk/how-to-obtain-a-phd-scholarship/admission-requirements/ .

  Please do not upload or submit recommendations, publications, theses, etc. 

  Assessment criteria
 The following criteria are applied when assessing PhD applications:

   	
• The quality, originality and feasibility of the PhD project and its relevance to the Sensing Korea project 	
• Research qualifications, as reflected in the attached CV and project description  	
• Competencies and knowledge of relevant fields of academic research 	
• Level (grades obtained) of Bachelor and Master’s studies.    Please note that only one position is available and competition is intense. 

  The recruitment process 
 After the deadline for applications, the Head of Department considers advice from the Appointment Committee and then selects applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether or not they have been shortlisted. After this, the Head of Department sets up an expert Assessment Committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Individual applicants will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Enrolment 
 It is a prerequisite for employment that successful applicants enrol at the PhD School of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. 
 For further information about the structure of the PhD programme, please refer to: Structure of the PhD programme – University of Copenhagen
 For further information about the guidelines for PhD studies at UCPH, please refer to: https://phd.ku.dk/english/

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range starts at approximately DKK 30,200 (EUR 4.040) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. According to the agreement, the PhD student is required to carry out tasks at the relevant department to an extent corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months). These tasks are primarily expected to consist of teaching in the department’s study programmes.

  You can read more about employment as a PhD Fellow here: Employment as a PhD student – University of Copenhagen.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk).

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in research, please visit: HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen.

  For further information about the application procedure, please refer to the University of Copenhagen website: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Contact Information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR South at: hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2541/26-2H.

We are seeking an experienced and practically minded Senior Consultant with a specialisation in climate to join our team and support large public- and private‑sector clients in planning and delivering credible decarbonisation and net‑zero strategies. • Advise on climate‑related disclosure and compliance (CSRD, TCFD/ISSB-aligned disclosures, CDP), and shape clients’ governance, risk management and climate strategy integration.
